questions.question_text: Which list contains all factors of $30$?

options.why: Omitted $15$, the partner of $2$ in $2 \times 15=30$.
Omitted $10$, the partner of $3$ in $3 \times 10=30$.
Omitted the number itself, which is always one of its factors.

questions.question_text: Which list contains all the factors of $28$?

options.why: Omitted $7$, the partner of $4$ in $4 \times 7=28$.
Omitted $28$, the number itself.
Included $56$, a multiple of $28$ rather than a factor.

questions.question_text: Which list contains all the factors of $35$?

options.why: Omitted $7$, the partner of $5$ in $5 \times 7=35$.
Omitted $1$, which is a factor of every positive whole number.
Included $70$, a multiple of $35$ rather than a factor.

questions.question_text: The factors of $45$ are $1,3,5,\square,15,45$. Which number fills the gap?

options.why: Subtracted $5$ from $45$ instead of dividing $45$ by $5$ to find its factor partner.
Repeated the listed factor $15$ instead of finding the missing partner of $5$.
Multiplied $45$ by $5$ instead of dividing $45$ by $5$.

questions.solution_text:
$5 \times 9=45$
The missing factor is $9$.
The complete list is $1,3,5,9,15,45$.

questions.question_text:
The factors of $42$ are listed as $1,2,3,6,14,21,42$.
Which factor is missing?

options.why: Gave the listed factor $6$ again instead of its missing partner in $6 \times 7=42$.
Subtracted the known factor $6$ from $42$ instead of dividing $42$ by $6$.
Multiplied $42$ by the known factor $6$ instead of finding its partner.

questions.question_text: Which list contains all the factors of $81$?

options.why: Omitted $9$, even though $9 \times 9=81$.
Listed $9$ twice because it appears twice in the pair $9 \times 9$.
Omitted $81$, the number itself.

questions.solution_text:
$1 \times 81$
$3 \times 27$
$9 \times 9$
Include $9$ only once in the factor list.
The factors are $1,3,9,27,81$.
